correctness.rationale: The theorem follows for all positive half-window lengths from cubic Binet identities, exact telescoping, endpoint parity identities, the reversible fourth-order recurrence for normalized T_a and U_a (characteristic constant term one), exact four-value GCDs, and 2/3/5 residue evaluations. The two affine GCDs divide 30; each local factor is determined from Lucas norm identity and Lucas cycles. Finite exact-integer verifier checked 320 sequence/window pairs, 1600 signed-sum reductions, 1001 arbitrary integer recurrence parameters, and k=6 discrepancy. The infinite result is proven algebraically; finite checks are not treated as extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The primary Mbirika--Spilker 2022 paper explicitly poses this cubic GCD problem in its Question 6.1 and gives a conjectural even-length Fibonacci formula that fails at k=6. Its proved theorems cover squares, not cubes. The new theorem proves exact GCD values for every even length for both Fibonacci and Lucas sequences. Related 2021 first-power and 2023 Pell/square papers do not imply this statement. Searches of mathematical literature, semantically indexed mathematical records, and accessible prior claim statements disclosed no equivalent or dominating result. This is best-evidence originality, not guaranteed absolute priority.
residual_risks: Unindexed or subsequent independent resolution of the posed cubic question may exist.
ArXiv final versions and related later papers beyond inspected mathematical sections could contain a correction or equivalent result.
The 2023 Pell paper and 2021 first-power paper were not exhaustively read; their accessible statements do not give this theorem.

value.rationale: Sliding-window power-sum GCDs are the central natural invariants of the 2021–2022 source sequence. The result completely determines every even third-power Fibonacci/Lucas GCD, answers its explicitly formulated cubic question in this setting, corrects a proposed formula with a concrete six-term counterexample, and explains the surprising powers of 2, 3 and 5 by a structural recurrence. A full infinite two-sequence classification is substantive and not a routine numerical instance.
